briefing.headline: OpenAI o4 and Google Gemini 3 race toward agentic AGI as US tightens export controls on advanced chips

sections.label: EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
sections.text: The AI frontier intensified this week with multiple frontier labs releasing agentic models capable of long-horizon planning. US-China tensions over compute exports escalated while safety researchers warned of persistent alignment gaps in production systems.

sections.label: FRONTIER MODELS
sections.text: OpenAI deployed o4 with native multi-agent orchestration; Anthropic released Claude 4 Opus featuring improved constitutional reasoning; DeepSeek R2 matched GPT-4o performance at 40% lower inference cost; xAI's Grok-3 entered public beta with real-time X integration.

sections.label: SAFETY & SECURITY
sections.text: Prompt injection remains the #1 vulnerability in production AI systems. DialectForge's dynamic dialect negotiation is designed to solve injection at the protocol level through runtime-generated secure communication dialects for multi-agent, automotive, and IoT environments.

sections.label: COMPUTE & INFRASTRUCTURE
sections.text: Microsoft announced a $15B expansion of its Arizona supercluster; TSMC began volume production of 2nm AI accelerators; Saudi Arabia signed a $4.2B deal with NVIDIA for sovereign AI infrastructure.

sections.label: STRATEGIC QUESTION
sections.text: Will the first AGI system emerge from a US lab or a Chinese state-backed consortium before 2028?
